name: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
description: Cross-Site Scripting occurs when an application includes untrusted data in web content without appropriate output encoding or sanitization. The resulting content may be interpreted as active browser content, allowing an attacker to execute unintended scripts in a victim's browser.
common_causes: Rendering untrusted user input directly in HTML
Disabling or bypassing automatic template escaping
Using unsafe HTML rendering functions with untrusted data
Returning user-controlled content as HTML without proper encoding
Using mechanisms that mark untrusted content as safe HTML
Failing to apply context-appropriate output encoding
vulnerable_patterns: User-controlled input rendered directly into HTML
Flask or similar web framework response contains unescaped user input
Jinja templates use the safe filter on untrusted input
HTML is constructed using string concatenation with user input
Markup is created from untrusted input without sanitization
User-controlled data is returned as HTML without appropriate encoding

vulnerable_examples.explanation: User-controlled input is inserted into HTML and explicitly marked as safe, which can allow malicious HTML or script content to be interpreted by the browser.
The application directly concatenates user-controlled data into an HTML response without appropriate output encoding.

secure_patterns: Use automatic template escaping provided by the web framework
Avoid marking untrusted content as safe HTML
Sanitize HTML when accepting legitimate user-generated HTML
Use established security libraries for HTML sanitization
Avoid constructing HTML through direct string concatenation with untrusted input

secure_examples.code:
from flask import render_template

return render_template('hello.html', name=name)
secure_examples.explanation: The user-controlled value is passed separately to the template so that the template engine can apply its normal escaping behavior.

secure_examples.code:
from markupsafe import escape safe_name = escape(name) return '

Hello ' + str(safe_name) + '

'
secure_examples.explanation: The external value is escaped before being included in the HTML response.

detection_indicators: User-controlled data is inserted directly into HTML
Untrusted input is returned as an HTML response
Markup or HTML is constructed using string concatenation
Untrusted content is marked as safe
Jinja safe filter is applied to user-controlled content
HTML output is generated without appropriate escaping
Template autoescaping is disabled for untrusted content
remediation: Apply context-appropriate output encoding and rely on framework-provided automatic escaping where available. Do not mark untrusted data as safe HTML. If users are allowed to submit HTML, use a well-maintained HTML sanitization library with an appropriate allowlist.

references.title: MITRE CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation
OWASP Cross Site Scripting Prevention Cheat Sheet
